A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LessIsMore by the same authors. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison despite the changed title and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original reasoning accuracies, attention-recall analyses, ablations, and decoding-latency measurements in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds model evaluations, long-context benchmarks, serving-stack measurements, kernel profiling, and layer-placement ablations.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 preserves per-head top-k proposals, unified aggregation, proportional recency preservation, and reuse of selected indices across layers. CUSA renames and explains the existing mechanism; the additional model evaluations and kernel measurements do not establish a changed selection algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds five LongBench tasks: MultiFieldQA, Qasper, HotpotQA, TriviaQA, and PassageRetrieval-en (Table 9), substantially broadening coverage beyond the retained reasoning benchmarks. Its extended long-context retrieval evaluation builds on Needle-in-the-Haystack diagnostics already present in v1.

E2.justification: StreamingLLM joins the Qwen reasoning-accuracy comparisons in v2 Figure 5, whereas v1 used it only in attention diagnostics. New retrieval comparisons evaluate H2O and TOVA alongside existing methods (Table 8), and Quest joins the decoding-latency comparison (Table 1).

E3.justification: Reasoning evaluation expands to Qwen3-14B and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, with additional non-reasoning GQA/MHA configurations and larger token budgets. Quest's reported block size changes from 64 to 32 for Qwen and 16 for DeepSeek. The Llama-3.1/A5000 timing setup is replaced by DeepSeek/A100 measurements and additional SGLang/A5000 tests.

E4.justification: v2 adds direct reasoning-accuracy ablations of re-selection placement, including no re-selection (Table 11), and recency-pattern analyses across GPQA/AIME-25 and token budgets (Figure 10). FLOP and memory-transfer profiling investigates the source of kernel efficiency. Earlier aggregation, recency-ratio, and generation-length analyses are largely retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Reported main-evaluation sampling increases from 16 to 64 traces per problem for AIME and from 8 to 16 for GPQA; MATH500 retains eight. Pass@1 remains the estimator, and no confidence intervals or significance tests are added. v2 Table 2 separately retains the older 16-trace generation-length analysis.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive model, budget, retrieval, LongBench, ablation, and efficiency results. Qwen3-8B/AIME-24 accuracy at 2K changes from 73.75 in v1 Table 2 to 73.00 in v2 Table 5 under increased sampling. Figure 6 newly reports up to 1.58x decoding and 1.72x kernel speedups under revised settings, rather than demonstrating a same-setting improvement over v1. The retained generation-length table changes only through rounding.

T1.justification: The attention, subset-selection, and attention-recall formulations remain equivalent, as does the algorithm's mathematical structure. Neither version develops formal theorems or proofs; v2's expanded stability arguments are empirical and conceptual.

C1.justification: v2 broadens the headline applicability claims to multiple model families, MHA architectures, and long-context tasks. The abstract and conclusion replace the earlier 1.1x average decoding and 1.13x end-to-end claims with up to 1.6x decoding acceleration over full attention and 1.72x sparse-kernel acceleration. The training-free unified-selection contribution remains.

C2.justification: v2 removes v1 Section 5's explicit discussion of fixed budgets and ratios, full-KV-cache memory costs, unoptimized index union, and extensions to MLA/MoE. It adds interpretations connecting kernel efficiency to reduced memory traffic and re-selection placement to semantic abstraction and attention stability (Appendices A.2 and A.5).

D1.justification: v2 documents SGLang/FlashInfer integration, identifies PG-19-mini for retrieval and layer selection, and summarizes model-specific re-selection layers in Table 10. v1's explicit disclosure that index aggregation uses PyTorch primitives disappears; this does not establish an implementation replacement. The code-access link remains unchanged.

R1.justification: References supporting LongBench, LongChat, TOVA, SGLang, and PagedAttention are added, while MagicPIG, Twilight, and Hymba are removed with the future-work discussion. The related-work taxonomy and central positioning against head-local selection and training-dependent sparse attention remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The title and terminology change, and the introduction, observations, and methodology are extensively rewritten around CUSA and global stability. Main-text ablations and locality discussions are reorganized into an expanded appendix, while the dedicated limitations section disappears and an impact statement is added.

P2.justification: The document switches from single-column to two-column layout. The method diagram is redrawn, the reasoning plot expands from eight to sixteen panels, and latency-accuracy plots are replaced by efficiency bar charts. Numerous tables and heatmaps are added; existing analyses are relocated or redisplayed, and detailed reasoning-baseline tables become compact LessIsMore/full-attention comparisons.

improvement.justification: v1's generality and efficiency claims relied mainly on two Qwen reasoning models and a separate Llama timing proxy. v2 substantially strengthens their validation through another reasoning family, MHA retrieval, LongBench, serving-stack measurements, memory profiling, and direct layer-placement ablations. These address important gaps in architectural generality, practical efficiency, and design justification. Removing explicit limitations and detailed baseline tables reduces transparency, but the targeted empirical additions provide a substantial net improvement.
